subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: Should OpenClaw keep Codex OAuth models on the Codex app-server and prove/fix the suspected app-server false-429 path, add direct OpenAI Responses Codex Harmony tool-call support as a supported fallback, or pursue both in stages?
rationale: The choice changes runtime ownership, provider routing, and tool-call parsing behavior, and source-only inspection cannot prove the live OAuth quota/app-server failure mode.

options.title: Investigate app-server first
options.body: Keep the documented Codex app-server default, land/finish the bookkeeping fix, and require live proof of the suspected app-server rate-limit/session behavior before routing changes.

options.title: Add direct Harmony adapter
options.body: Implement direct OpenAI Responses support for Codex Harmony tool calls and then evaluate direct runtime as an explicit fallback for Codex OAuth models.

options.title: Stage both paths
options.body: Treat #99810 as the immediate bookkeeping repair while opening a separate maintainer-owned runtime project for app-server proof and direct adapter validation.

recommendation.title: Investigate app-server first
recommendation.body: Keep the documented Codex app-server default, land/finish the bookkeeping fix, and require live proof of the suspected app-server rate-limit/session behavior before routing changes.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged work across OpenAI provider identity, Codex harness routing, and direct OpenAI transport, which is the decision surface for this issue.
